_note: Domain events and their subscriber scripts. Lifecycle wiring lives in .claude/settings.json; this file documents intent. Scripts read their payload via _hooklib.load_payload(), so both Claude Code (stdin) and tools/run_hook.py work. Every hook here ACTS or DENIES. Hooks whose only output was the name of a skill were deleted on 2026-08-04: hooks and skills are independent, a hook cannot invoke a skill, and a skill name written into hook source is an unvalidated second copy of a routing decision. Skills trigger from their own `description:` frontmatter.

session-start.description: At session start; loads the knowledge docs into session context

post-run.description: After a turn completes; snapshots recovery state, then commits the turn as a wip checkpoint if the artefact gates pass

pre-commit.description: Before a git commit/push finalizes; refuses credentials and protected-branch commits

pre-edit.description: Before a file write; refuses generated, vendored and lockfile targets

pre-deploy.description: Before a cloud-CLI command; allowlist-first free-tier spend guard

on-artifact-create.description: After a hook script is edited; demands it be fired against a real payload before being trusted

global-session-start.description: At session start in ANY repo; installs this layer into the session's directory if and only if it is a git repo root, outside this repo, with no .claude/skills/ and no foreign .claude/agents/ or .claude/hooks/. ACTS, and speaks when it acts, when it fails, and on the two near misses a user can act on.
global-session-start._note: Deliberately absent from this repo's .claude/settings.json and therefore exempt from the on-disk-must-be-wired check. It is wired in ~/.claude/settings.json by absolute path, because a project hook only fires inside its own project -- which is the opposite of what this one is for. `tools/test_hook_registration.py` checks the global wiring separately, and skips with a spoken reason where ~/.claude/settings.json does not exist (CI).
